claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Ablation of ZNF598 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
claims.source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Ablation of the ribosomal protein RACK1 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
claims.source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Mutation of conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
claims.source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Mutation of conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
claims.source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Ribosome collisions are the key initiation signal which recruits critical ubiquitin ligases to facilitate RRub.
claims.source: Current models suggest that ribosome collisions are the key initiation signal which recruits critical ubiquitin ligases to facilitate RRub allowing for subsequent nascent chain ubiquitylation, mRNA degradation, and ribosome recycling (Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Simms et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Simms et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Both uS10 and eS10 ubiquitylation are required for mammalian RQC.
claims.source: The observation that both uS10 and eS10 ubiquitylation are required for mammalian RQC suggest a potential structured order of ubiquitylation events may be needed to specifically mark collided ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from prior studies and the authors' own data.

claims.claim: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in mammalian cells triggers RRub events on uS3 (RPS3) and uS5 (RPS2) that do not require ZNF598.
claims.source: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in mammalian cells triggers an additional set of RRub events on uS3 (RPS3) and uS5 (RPS2) that do not require ZNF598 and do not function within the RQC pathway and whose function remains uncharacterized (Higgins et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015).

claims.claim: ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 RRub events do not function within the RQC pathway.
claims.source: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in mammalian cells triggers an additional set of RRub events on uS3 (RPS3) and uS5 (RPS2) that do not require ZNF598 and do not function within the RQC pathway and whose function remains uncharacterized (Higgins et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015).

claims.claim: The extent of ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 monoubiquitylation diminished upon removal of ISR agonists.
claims.source: Studies in mammalian cells have demonstrated that the extent of ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 monoubiquitylation diminished upon removal of ISR agonists (Higgins et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015).

claims.claim: ANS induced ubiquitylation of both eS10 and uS10.
claims.source: Consistent with previous studies, ANS induced ubiquitylation of both eS10 and uS10 (Figure 1A; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017).

claims.claim: eS10 ubiquitylation diminished over time during ANS treatment.
claims.source: While eS10 ubiquitylation diminished and uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time, there was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of the unmodified form of each protein (Figure 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claims.claim: uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time during ANS treatment.
claims.source: While eS10 ubiquitylation diminished and uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time, there was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of the unmodified form of each protein (Figure 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claims.claim: There was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of unmodified eS10 or uS10 during ANS treatment.
claims.source: While eS10 ubiquitylation diminished and uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time, there was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of the unmodified form of each protein (Figure 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claims.claim: No accumulation of unmodified or ubiquitylated eS10 or uS10 was observed with combined treatment of proteasome inhibitors and ANS over 12 hr.
claims.source: Further no accumulation of unmodified or ubiquitylated eS10 or uS10 was observed with combined treatment of proteasome inhibitors and ANS over 12 hr indicating that ribosomal proteins are either not rapidly degraded when ribosome stalling is stimulated, or degradation cannot be detected within the limit of immunoblotting approaches used in these experiments.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Figure 1A.

claims.claim: DTT stimulated uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation which subsequently diminished to pre-treatment levels over time.
claims.source: DTT stimulated uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation which subsequently diminished to pre-treatment levels over time (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: The relative amount of unmodified uS5 and uS3 protein remained stable despite global protein synthesis attenuation.
claims.source: Further, the relative amount of the unmodified protein remained stable despite global protein synthesis attenuation (Figure 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claims.claim: UV exposure stimulates uS5, uS3, eS10 and uS10 regulatory ubiquitylation.
claims.source: To further examine the reversibility and timing of distinct RRub events, we utilized UV-induced ISR activation which stimulates uS5, uS3, eS10 and uS10 regulatory ubiquitylation (Elia et al., 2015; Higgins et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Elia et al., 2015; Higgins et al., 2015).

claims.claim: All observed RRub events diminished over time following UV exposure.
claims.source: All observed RRub events diminished over time further indicating the RRub events are reversible (Figure 1E,F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claims.claim: eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation preceded uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation after UV exposure.
claims.source: Interestingly, eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation preceded uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation after UV exposure (Figure 1E,F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claims.claim: ISR-stimulated uS5 and uS3 RRub events require eIF2α phosphorylation.
claims.source: Consistent with previous studies demonstrating that ISR-stimulated uS5 and uS3 RRub events require eIF2α phosphorylation, uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation occurred coincidently with eIF2α phosphorylation (Higgins et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015) and experimental data from Figure 1E.

claims.claim: uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation occurred coincidently with eIF2α phosphorylation following UV exposure.
claims.source: Consistent with previous studies demonstrating that ISR-stimulated uS5 and uS3 RRub events require eIF2α phosphorylation, uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation occurred coincidently with eIF2α phosphorylation (Higgins et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Mutating RRub lysine residues in eS10 K138R/K139R did not result in altered protein stability following ANS treatment.
claims.source: We observed no appreciable change in total protein abundance in the eS10 K138R/K139R knock-in (eS10-KI) and uS10 K4R/K8R knock-in (uS10-KI) cells following ANS treatment (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: Mutating RRub lysine residues in uS10 K4R/K8R did not result in altered protein stability following ANS treatment.
claims.source: We observed no appreciable change in total protein abundance in the eS10 K138R/K139R knock-in (eS10-KI) and uS10 K4R/K8R knock-in (uS10-KI) cells following ANS treatment (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: The inability to ubiquitylate uS5 K54R/K58R did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS5.
claims.source: Similarly, the inability to ubiquitylate uS5 K54R/K58R (uS5-KI) and uS3 K214R (uS3-KI) did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS5 or uS3 (Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: The inability to ubiquitylate uS3 K214R did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS3.
claims.source: Similarly, the inability to ubiquitylate uS5 K54R/K58R (uS5-KI) and uS3 K214R (uS3-KI) did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS5 or uS3 (Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: eS10-KI cell lines completely lack ANS-induced eS10 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: As expected, eS10-KI cell lines completely lack ANS-induced eS10 ubiquitylation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Loss of eS10 ubiquitylation substantially reduces uS10 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: However, loss of eS10 ubiquitylation substantially reduces uS10 ubiquitylation (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) as compared to control cell lines.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: The inability to ubiquitylate eS10 had a negligible impact on the levels of UV-induced uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: The inability to ubiquitylate eS10 had a negligible impact on the levels of UV-induced uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: uS10-KI cells maintained their ability to ubiquitylate eS10, uS5, and uS3 despite the loss of uS10 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: In contrast, uS10-KI cells maintained their ability to ubiquitylate eS10, uS5, and uS3 despite the expected loss of uS10 ubiquitylation (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The lack of DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation in the uS3-KI cells results in complete ablation of uS5 modification.
claims.source: Similar to the hierarchy of eS10 and uS10, the lack of DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation in the uS3-KI cells results in complete ablation of uS5 modification while loss of uS5 ubiquitylation did not effect uS3 DTT-stimulated RRub (Figure 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claims.claim: Loss of uS5 ubiquitylation did not effect uS3 DTT-stimulated RRub.
claims.source: Similar to the hierarchy of eS10 and uS10, the lack of DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation in the uS3-KI cells results in complete ablation of uS5 modification while loss of uS5 ubiquitylation did not effect uS3 DTT-stimulated RRub (Figure 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claims.claim: Loss of ZNF598 function results in readthrough of poly(A) sequences and a subsequent increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter.
claims.source: Previous studies demonstrated that loss of ZNF598 function and the resulting decrease in eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation results in readthrough of poly(A) sequences and a subsequent increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Expression of OTUB2, OTUD3, USP10 and UCHL1 did not alter the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter.
claims.source: OTUB2, OTUD3, USP10 and UCHL1 expression did not alter the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter while OTUD1 and USP21 only modestly elevated the ChFP:GFP ratio indicating that the identified Dubs specifically alter the ability of ribosomes to progress through a poly(A)-induced ribosomal stall (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: OTUD1 and USP21 only modestly elevated the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter.
claims.source: OTUB2, OTUD3, USP10 and UCHL1 expression did not alter the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter while OTUD1 and USP21 only modestly elevated the ChFP:GFP ratio indicating that the identified Dubs specifically alter the ability of ribosomes to progress through a poly(A)-induced ribosomal stall (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Expression of inactive OTUD3 or USP21 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
claims.source: In contrast, expression of the inactive mutants for the deubiquitylating enzymes USP21, OTUD3, and USP10 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Expression of inactive USP10 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
claims.source: In contrast, expression of the inactive mutants for the deubiquitylating enzymes USP21, OTUD3, and USP10 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Expression of inactive OTUD3 or USP21 resulted in elevated stall readthrough compared to control transfections.
claims.source: Expression of inactive OTUD3 or USP21 resulted in elevated stall readthrough compared to control transfections indicating a possible alternative role for OTUD3 and USP21 within the RQC pathway that is ZNF598 independent.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Exogenous expression of wild type ZNF598 resulted in decreased ChFP:GFP ratios as compared to control transfections.
claims.source: As expected, exogenous expression of wild type ZNF598 resulted in decreased ChFP:GFP ratios as compared to control transfections (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: USP21 and OTUD3, when co-expressed with ZNF598, resulted in a greater than 2.5 fold increase in the ChFP:GFP poly(A) reporter ratio relative to what was observed when ZNF598 was expressed in isolation.
claims.source: Both USP21 and OTUD3, when co-expressed with ZNF598, resulted in a greater than 2.5 fold increase in the ChFP:GFP poly(A) reporter ratio relative to what was observed when ZNF598 was expressed in isolation (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Cells solely overexpressing ZNF598 displayed a 5-fold increase in the abundance of ubiquitylated eS10 compared to untransfected cells.
claims.source: Immunoblot analysis revealed that cells solely overexpressing ZNF598 displayed a 5-fold increase in the abundance of ubiquitylated eS10 compared to untransfected cells (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: Exogenous expression of USP21 substantially reduced the ZNF598-stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in an activity-dependent manner.
claims.source: Exogenous expression of USP21 substantially reduced the ZNF598-stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in an activity-dependent manner (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: Exogenous expression of OTUD3 substantially reduced the ZNF598-stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: The same result was observed upon expression of OTUD3 and ZNF598 (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: ZNF598-KO cells displayed elevated ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter.
claims.source: ZNF598-KO cells displayed the expected elevated ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter which was modestly enhanced upon further expression of either Dub (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: Expression of USP21 or OTUD3 in ZNF598-KO cells modestly enhanced the ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter.
claims.source: ZNF598-KO cells displayed the expected elevated ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter which was modestly enhanced upon further expression of either Dub (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: eS10-KI and uS10-KI cell lines allowed for enhanced readthrough of poly(A)-mediated stall events using the stall reporter FACS assay.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous results, eS10-KI and uS10-KI cell lines allowed for enhanced readthrough of poly(A)-mediated stall events using our stall reporter FACS assay whereas uS3-KI and uS5-KI cell lines did not appreciably alter reporter levels compared to parental cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and citation to prior work (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claims.claim: uS3-KI and uS5-KI cell lines did not appreciably alter reporter levels compared to parental cells.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous results, eS10-KI and uS10-KI cell lines allowed for enhanced readthrough of poly(A)-mediated stall events using our stall reporter FACS assay whereas uS3-KI and uS5-KI cell lines did not appreciably alter reporter levels compared to parental cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: USP21 or OTUD3 overexpression in either eS10-KI or uS10-KI cells resulted in a further enhancement of the ChFP:GFP ratio above the respective transfection controls.
claims.source: USP21 or OTUD3 overexpression in either eS10-KI or uS10-KI cells resulted in a further enhancement of the ChFP:GFP ratio above the respective transfection controls (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claims.claim: Expression of inactive OTUD3 reduced the extent of readthrough compared to wild type in both eS10 and uS10 knock-in cell lines.
claims.source: This enhancement was largely activity-dependent as expression of inactive OTUD3 reduced the extent of readthrough compared to wild type in both eS10 and uS10 knock-in cell lines (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Expression of inactive USP21 resulted in reduced readthrough compared to wild type in uS10-KI cells but not eS10-KI cells.
claims.source: Expression of inactive USP21 resulted in reduced readthrough compared to wild type in uS10-KI cells but not eS10-KI cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The combined loss of uS10 and eS10 RRub events results in a stronger RQC defect than loss of either uS10 or eS10 ubiquitylation events alone.
claims.source: These results indicate that OTUD3 and USP21 can demodify both uS10 and eS10, consistent with our immunoblotting data (Figure 3E). Further, these results indicate that the combined loss of uS10 and eS10 RRub events results in a stronger RQC defect than loss of either uS10 or eS10 ubiquitylation events alone.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing enhanced readthrough in knock-in cells with Dub overexpression.

claims.claim: ZNF598 expression stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in parental HCT116 cells.
claims.source: As expected, ZNF598 expression stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in parental HCT116 cells (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: ZNF598 expression in uS10-KI cells failed to induce uS10 ubiquitylation without impacting the ability of ZNF598 to ubiquitylate eS10.
claims.source: ZNF598 expression in uS10-KI cells failed to induce uS10 ubiquitylation without impacting the ability of ZNF598 to ubiquitylate eS10.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: ZNF598 expression failed to ubiquitylate eS10 in eS10-KI cells, and uS10 ubiquitylation was substantially reduced compared to ZNF598 expression in parental cells.
claims.source: Conversely, ZNF598 expression failed to ubiquitylate eS10 in eS10-KI cells, and uS10 ubiquitylation was substantially reduced compared to ZNF598 expression in parental cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Expression of wild type USP21 or OTUD3 reduced the abundance of both monoubiquitylated eS10 and uS10 in parental HCT116 cells.
claims.source: While expression of wild type USP21 or OTUD3 reduced the abundance of both monoubiquitylated eS10 and uS10 in parental HCT116 cells, expression of the inactive variants restored ubiquitylation to steady-state levels (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Expression of inactive USP21 or OTUD3 variants restored ubiquitylation to steady-state levels.
claims.source: While expression of wild type USP21 or OTUD3 reduced the abundance of both monoubiquitylated eS10 and uS10 in parental HCT116 cells, expression of the inactive variants restored ubiquitylation to steady-state levels (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: ZNF598 protein levels are 19-fold in excess of OTUD3.
claims.source: Examination of quantitative proteomic datasets from human cell lines revealed that ZNF598 protein levels are 19-fold in excess of OTUD3 while USP21 levels were undetectable indicating that ZNF598 protein levels are in vast excess of either RRub Dub at steady state (Itzhak et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Itzhak et al., 2016).

claims.claim: USP21 levels were undetectable in quantitative proteomic datasets from human cell lines.
claims.source: Examination of quantitative proteomic datasets from human cell lines revealed that ZNF598 protein levels are 19-fold in excess of OTUD3 while USP21 levels were undetectable indicating that ZNF598 protein levels are in vast excess of either RRub Dub at steady state (Itzhak et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Itzhak et al., 2016).

claims.claim: Expression of the poly(A)-reporter with increasing concentrations of exogenous ZNF598 in isolation did not result in a dose-dependent decrease in the ChFP:GFP ratio.
claims.source: Expression of the poly(A)-reporter with increasing concentrations of exogenous ZNF598 in isolation did not result in a dose-dependent decrease in the ChFP:GFP ratio suggesting that ZNF598 expression at the lowest levels tested were sufficient to fully restore RQC function and that elevated ZNF598 levels do not further enhance ribosome stall resolution (Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D.

claims.claim: When equal amounts of USP21 or OTUD3 and ZNF598 expression plasmids were transfected, a substantial increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio was observed as compared to ZNF598 expressed alone.
claims.source: When equal amounts of USP21 or OTUD3 and ZNF598 expression plasmids were transfected, a substantial increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio was observed as compared to ZNF598 expressed alone which further verified the direct antagonism observed previously (Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D.

claims.claim: The reporter ChFP:GFP ratio declined as ZNF598 plasmid transfections were doubled and tripled with respect to USP21 or OTUD3 plasmid DNA.
claims.source: The reporter ChFP:GFP ratio declined as ZNF598 plasmid transfections were doubled and tripled with respect to USP21 or OTUD3 plasmid DNA (Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D.

claims.claim: Doubling and tripling the expression of USP21 while holding ZNF598 expression levels constant revealed additional readthrough of the poly(A) stall-inducing sequence with increasing ChFP:GFP ratios.
claims.source: Conversely, doubling and tripling the expression of USP21 while holding ZNF598 expression levels constant revealed additional readthrough of the poly(A) stall-inducing sequence with increasing ChFP:GFP ratios, suggesting further antagonism of the ligase.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: In cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, the amount of detectable eS10 ubiquitylation rapidly declined 1 hr post UV exposure.
claims.source: Interestingly, in cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, the amount of detectable eS10 ubiquitylation rapidly declined 1 hr post UV exposure, while uS10 ubiquitylation was completely ablated (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: In cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, uS10 ubiquitylation was completely ablated following UV exposure.
claims.source: Interestingly, in cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, the amount of detectable eS10 ubiquitylation rapidly declined 1 hr post UV exposure, while uS10 ubiquitylation was completely ablated (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The dynamics of eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment in cells expressing inactive USP21 were unaltered compared to cells without Dox-treatment.
claims.source: Immunoblots confirmed that the dynamics of eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment in cells expressing inactive USP21 were unaltered compared to cells without Dox-treatment. (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: OTUD3 expression resulted in substantially reduced eS10 ubiquitylation and complete ablation of uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment compared to uninduced cells.
claims.source: Similar to what was observed upon USP21 expression, OTUD3 expression resulted in substantially reduced eS10 ubiquitylation and complete ablation of uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment compared to uninduced cells (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Induction of inactive OTUD3 did not alter either eS10 or uS10 ubiquitylation upon UV treatment.
claims.source: This reduction in eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation was activity dependent as induction of inactive OTUD3 did not alter either eS10 or uS10 ubiquitylation upon UV treatment (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Two separate knockout clones for both USP21 and OTUD3 displayed reduced poly(A)-mediated stall readthrough.
claims.source: Two separate knockout clones for both USP21 and OTUD3 displayed reduced poly(A)-mediated stall readthrough which is consistent with our demonstration that overexpression of OTUD3 or USP21 enhances stall readthrough (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Combined loss of USP21 and OTUD3 did not further reduce stall readthrough compared to individual knockouts.
claims.source: Combined loss of USP21 and OTUD3 did not further reduce stall readthrough compared to individual knockouts suggesting that the Dubs may be acting at distinct points within the RQC pathway (Figure 6A).

results.result: Regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation (RRub) events are reversible and diminish over time following stress stimuli. The authors demonstrate that RRub levels decrease without corresponding protein degradation, suggesting deubiquitylating enzymes mediate this reversibility rather than protein turnover.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C38-C43, and C45 provide converging experimental evidence from multiple stress conditions (ANS, DTT, UV) showing time-dependent reduction in RRub levels without corresponding changes in unmodified protein levels. The lack of protein accumulation with proteasome inhibitors (C41) supports the deubiquitylation mechanism over degradation. This is a well-controlled set of experiments with consistent results across different stressors.

results.result: A hierarchical relationship exists among RRub events where uS10 ubiquitylation depends on eS10 ubiquitylation, and uS5 ubiquitylation depends on uS3 ubiquitylation. This establishes a sequential ubiquitin code on ribosomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C4 and C54, C57-C58 are strongly supported by knock-in experiments showing that loss of eS10 ubiquitylation substantially reduces uS10 modification (Figure 2A), and loss of uS3 ubiquitylation completely ablates uS5 modification (Figure 2C,D). The reciprocal experiments (uS10-KI and uS5-KI) show no effect on upstream targets, confirming directionality. This hierarchical relationship is reproducible and well-documented.

results.result: OTUD3 and USP21 are deubiquitylating enzymes that antagonize ZNF598-mediated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation and can limit RQC activation. Overexpression of these Dubs increases poly(A) stall readthrough and reduces ZNF598-stimulated ubiquitylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C11 and C68-C69 are supported by multiple complementary assays: the poly(A) stall reporter showing increased readthrough (Figure 3), immunoblotting demonstrating reduced eS10/uS10 ubiquitylation upon Dub overexpression (Figure 3E), and co-expression experiments showing antagonism of ZNF598 (Figure 3D). The activity-dependent nature is confirmed with catalytically inactive mutants. The evidence is robust and internally consistent.

results.result: Loss of USP21 or OTUD3 function results in altered RQC activity and delayed eS10 deubiquitylation following stress. Knockout cells show reduced poly(A) stall readthrough and sustained eS10 ubiquitylation up to 24 hours post-UV exposure.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C15 and C94-C98 are supported by loss-of-function experiments using knockout cell lines. Figure 6A shows reduced stall readthrough in knockout cells, and Figure 6B demonstrates delayed deubiquitylation kinetics. The use of multiple independent knockout clones strengthens the findings. However, the authors note that siRNA knockdown was insufficient to observe phenotypes, requiring complete genetic ablation, which suggests the phenotype may be subtle or that compensatory mechanisms exist.

results.result: Overexpression of wild-type USP21 or OTUD3 results in accelerated removal of ubiquitin from eS10 and uS10 following UV-induced RQC in an activity-dependent manner.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C93 and C106 are supported by experiments using doxycycline-inducible cell lines (Figure 5). Wild-type Dub expression leads to rapid deubiquitylation of eS10 and complete ablation of uS10 ubiquitylation, while inactive mutants show no effect. The activity-dependence is clearly demonstrated, and the use of inducible systems provides good temporal control. The experiments are well-controlled with appropriate inactive mutant comparisons.

results.result: The relative abundance of ZNF598 versus USP21/OTUD3 governs RQC activity. Increasing ZNF598 levels relative to Dubs reduces stall readthrough, while increasing Dub levels enhances readthrough, demonstrating dose-dependent antagonism.
results.evaluation: Claims C66 and C85-C88 are supported by titration experiments (Figure 4F,G) showing that the ChFP:GFP ratio changes predictably with varying ratios of ZNF598 to Dub expression plasmids. This demonstrates quantitative antagonism. The observation that ZNF598 is naturally 19-fold more abundant than OTUD3 (C83) provides physiological context. The dose-response relationship is clear and reproducible.

results.result: Combinatorial ubiquitylation of both eS10 and uS10 is required for optimal RQC function. Overexpression of Dubs in knock-in cell lines lacking either eS10 or uS10 ubiquitylation sites results in enhanced stall readthrough beyond that observed with single mutations alone.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 and C108-C109 are supported by experiments combining knock-in mutations with Dub overexpression (Figure 4C,D). The observation that Dub overexpression further enhances readthrough in cells already lacking one ubiquitylation site demonstrates that both modifications contribute independently to RQC function. The activity-dependence is confirmed with inactive mutants. This provides strong evidence for a combinatorial ubiquitin code.

results.result: USP21 has broader substrate specificity than OTUD3, deubiquitylating both RQC-associated (eS10, uS10) and ISR-associated (uS3, uS5) ribosomal proteins, while OTUD3 primarily targets RQC substrates.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C100 and C107 are supported by experiments testing Dub activity against different RRub substrates (Figure 7A,B). USP21 reduces ubiquitylation of all four tested ribosomal proteins in an activity-dependent manner, while OTUD3 only affects uS5 (modestly) and has no impact on uS3. This differential substrate specificity is clearly demonstrated and suggests distinct functional roles for the two Dubs.

results.result: OTUD3 associates with ribosomes and is preferentially localized to 40S-containing fractions rather than 80S or polysomes, suggesting it acts on split ribosomal subunits during late RQC events.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C102 are supported by biochemical fractionation data (Figure 7C-E) showing OTUD3 in ribosome pellets and 40S fractions. However, C103 is speculative inference about the functional significance of this localization. While the localization data is clear, the interpretation that OTUD3 acts as a 'late step' during RQC requires additional functional validation. The authors appropriately use cautious language ('may preferentially'), but the mechanistic conclusion remains uncertain.

results.result: Following UV exposure, eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation precedes uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation, with the latter occurring coincident with eIF2α phosphorylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C48 are supported by time-course experiments following UV exposure (Figure 1E,F). The temporal separation between RQC-associated (eS10/uS10) and ISR-associated (uS3/uS5) ubiquitylation events is clearly demonstrated. The correlation with eIF2α phosphorylation is consistent with prior work (C47) and observed in the data. This temporal analysis provides insight into the sequential activation of different stress response pathways.

results.result: Mutation of RRub lysine residues in eS10, uS10, uS5, or uS3 does not alter the stability or steady-state abundance of these ribosomal proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C52 are supported by experiments in knock-in cell lines showing no appreciable changes in total protein abundance (Figure 2A-D and supplements). This is an important control demonstrating that the ubiquitylation events are regulatory rather than degradative. The experiments include proteasome inhibitor treatments to rule out rapid turnover. This supports the non-degradative role of monoubiquitylation.

results.result: Expression of USP21 or OTUD3 in ZNF598 knockout cells modestly enhances poly(A) stall readthrough beyond the elevated baseline observed in ZNF598-KO cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C71 are supported by experiments in ZNF598-KO cells (Figure 4A,B). The modest enhancement suggests ZNF598-independent functions for these Dubs. However, the authors note this modest effect is also observed with other Dubs and may be partially non-specific. The interpretation of ZNF598-independent activity is reasonable but should be considered preliminary.

results.result: eS10-KI and uS10-KI cell lines show enhanced poly(A) stall readthrough, while uS3-KI and uS5-KI cell lines do not alter readthrough compared to parental cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C73 are supported by FACS-based reporter assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G). This confirms that eS10/uS10 ubiquitylation is required for RQC function while uS3/uS5 ubiquitylation is not, consistent with their distinct roles in ISR versus RQC pathways. This validates the knock-in cell lines and confirms prior findings from the literature.

results.result: ZNF598 protein levels are 19-fold in excess of OTUD3, while USP21 levels are undetectable in quantitative proteomic datasets from human cell lines.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C84 are supported by citation to published proteomic data (Itzhak et al., 2016). This provides important physiological context for the antagonism experiments, suggesting that under normal conditions, ZNF598 activity predominates. However, this is based on a single cited dataset and the authors' own overexpression experiments required 40-100 fold overexpression to compete with endogenous ZNF598.

results.result: Combined loss of USP21 and OTUD3 does not further reduce stall readthrough compared to individual knockouts.
results.evaluation: Claim C95 is supported by experiments with double knockout cells (Figure 6A). The lack of additivity suggests the Dubs may act at the same step or that a threshold effect exists. The authors interpret this as evidence for distinct action points, but alternative explanations (saturation, compensatory mechanisms) are possible. The observation is clear but the mechanistic interpretation is speculative.

results.result: Background claims establishing prior knowledge about ISR, RQC pathways, and regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation from the literature.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1-C2, C16-C37, C44, C59) are supported by appropriate citations to prior work and represent established knowledge in the field. They provide necessary context for the current study but are not novel findings. The authors accurately represent prior work and cite appropriate references.
